\textbf{Quiz 2}

\vspace{2em}

\textbf{Multiple Choice Questions (Single correct)}\\[0.5em]
\emph{Instructions: Select the correct option with a short explanation.}

\begin{enumerate}[label=Q\arabic*., leftmargin=*]
\item \duallayerbox{What is the main difference between generative and discriminative classifiers?}{Which model type focuses on modeling P(y | x) directly for classification?}\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} Generative models model $P(x, y)$, while discriminative models model $P(y \mid x)$\\
\textbf{B.} Discriminative models learn the data distribution and use that knowledge for classification\\
\textbf{C.} Discriminative models require no training data\\
\textbf{D.} Generative models are less explainable

\item \duallayerbox{Which technique is used to mitigate overfitting by penalizing large weights?}{Which technique assigns higher importance to rare but informative terms in documents?}\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} Laplace smoothing\\
\textbf{B.} Regularization\\
\textbf{C.} TF-IDF\\
\textbf{D.} Softmax normalization

\item \duallayerbox{What is the limitation of the perceptron algorithm?}{Which option describes a classifier that succeeds only when classes are perfectly separable?}\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} It cannot use vector representations\\
\textbf{B.} It only works for linearly separable data\\
\textbf{C.} It requires probabilistic outputs\\
\textbf{D.} It cannot be trained with gradient descent

\item Why is Laplace smoothing important?\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} It improves cosine similarity\\
\textbf{B.} It reduces dimensionality\\
\textbf{C.} It avoids zero probabilities for unseen words\\
\textbf{D.} It speeds up gradient descent

\item What happens in stochastic gradient descent (SGD) compared to gradient descent (GD)?\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} SGD updates weights using the entire dataset every step\\
\textbf{B.} SGD updates weights using one or a subset of training examples\\
\textbf{C.} GD converges faster because updates are noisier\\
\textbf{D.} SGD cannot be used with neural networks

\item What is the core intuition behind word embeddings?\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} Words are represented by their dictionary definitions\\
\textbf{B.} Words that appear in similar contexts have similar meanings\\
\textbf{C.} Words are clustered by part of speech\\
\textbf{D.} Words are ranked by frequency

\item What is the primary purpose of the Softmax function?\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} To penalize large model weights\\
\textbf{B.} To reduce feature dimensionality\\
\textbf{C.} To select the class with the largest raw score without normalization\\
\textbf{D.} To convert raw class scores into a valid probability distribution

\item In the perceptron algorithm, when are the weights updated?\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} After every training example\\
\textbf{B.} Only when the prediction is correct\\
\textbf{C.} Only when the prediction is incorrect\\
\textbf{D.} Only after one full pass over the data

\item What is the main goal of TF-IDF weighting?\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} Increase the weight of very common words\\
\textbf{B.} Represent word order\\
\textbf{C.} Convert sparse vectors into dense embeddings\\
\textbf{D.} Highlight words that are frequent in a document but rare across documents

\item Why is cosine similarity preferred over dot product when comparing word vectors?\\[0.25em]
\textbf{A.} It ignores vector length while calculating similarity\\
\textbf{B.} It increases the influence of high-frequency words\\
\textbf{C.} It converts similarity scores into probabilities\\
\textbf{D.} It reduces the dimensionality of word embeddings

\end{enumerate}
